company.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

profile_text.body:
The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, known as Stanford HAI, is a nonprofit university lab founded in 2019 and based at Stanford, California. It describes its work as advancing AI research, education, and policy to improve the human condition, and defines human-centered AI as an approach that prioritizes human needs, values, and well-being throughout the development and deployment of AI systems. Fei-Fei Li and John Etchemendy are named as Denning Co-Directors. The institute says it was established to support research that bridges disciplines, including fellowship programs for researchers working at intersections often overlooked by traditional academic departments.

Its site lists grant programs, courses for leaders and decision-makers, specialized training for policymakers and civil servants, and education work aimed at the K-12 ecosystem, teachers, and students, along with affinity groups for students. It publishes an annual AI Index, which it describes as reporting a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared institutions are to manage it, alongside declining data transparency. Erik Brynjolfsson, director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab and a senior fellow at Stanford HAI, is quoted arguing that businesses gain more from AI used to support employees' productivity than from replacing workers. Other items on the site include a Stanford research finding that users with limited social networks who seek emotional support from AI companions report lower well-being, Clinical Mind AI, described as a Stanford-developed international platform using AI-simulated patient encounters for clinical reasoning education, presented by Marcos Santiago Rojas Pino and Thomas Caruso, and a Joint California Summit on Generative AI highlighted in Governor Newsom's Executive Order. Stanford Law School researchers are also described as building an AI pipeline to comb through millions of local statutes.

The institute is not associated with any tracked products, lawsuits, or MCP servers. Its recorded regulatory exposure is in California, with a count of 281.
